title: Integrating Silicon and Plant-Residue Mulching in Yellow Passion Fruit under Semiarid Conditions: Effects on Leaf Physiology, Yield, and Fruit Quality
content: High evaporative demand under semiarid conditions can constrain leaf hydration and carbon assimilation in yellow passion fruit, motivating integrated silicon fertilization and soil mulching strategies. This study evaluated soil-applied silicon (Si) and plant-residue mulch effects on physiology, yield, and fruit quality of Passiflora edulis Sims. A field experiment used a randomized complete block design with a 5 × 2 factorial arrangement, comprising five Si doses (0, 27, 54, 81, and 108 g plant⁻¹), two mulch conditions (presence and absence), and four replicates. Mulch consisted of Cenchrus ciliaris and Megathyrsus maximus residues. Mulched plants exhibited higher predicted stomatal conductance and CO₂ assimilation and lower transpiration throughout the evaluated dose range. Increasing Si doses increased relative water content and reduced electrolyte leakage under both conditions. Maximum predicted yields were 31.29 t ha⁻¹ with mulch at 58.06 g plant⁻¹ and 21.64 t ha⁻¹ without mulch at 55.12 g plant⁻¹. With mulch, maximum predicted average fruit mass and seedless pulp mass reached 327.86 and 114.68 g, respectively. Pulp pH, titratable acidity, total soluble solids, and the TSS/TA ratio showed quadratic responses. Intermediate Si doses combined with plant-residue mulch favored yield, whereas doses associated with maximum physiological responses and fruit attributes differed.
